cards.text: Friend, the Jews are in danger: Haman has promised money to the king's treasury to destroy them, and Mordecai has begged Queen Esther to go plead with the king for her people. Problem is, walking in on the king without being summoned can get you put to death, and she hasn't been called in thirty days. So the Jews in Susa fast, Esther fasts with them, and she says, "And if I perish, I perish!"

On the third day, Esther puts on her royal robes and stands in the inner court, right across from the king's quarters. The king is on his throne, facing the entrance, so there is NO sneaking in on this man.

cards.question: As soon as the king sees Esther standing in the court uninvited, she finds favor in his sight.
The king holds out the gold ___ in his hand toward Esther, and she comes forward and touches its tip.

cards.text: She's still standing, friend. Everybody breathe. Then the king asks, "What is it, Queen Esther?" and he makes her an offer.

cards.question: The king asks Esther what her request is. How much is he willing to give her?
With up to half the kingdom on the table, what does Esther ask the king for?

answers.text: The king and Haman at her banquet today
An end to the law against the Jews
A pardon for Mordecai at the gate

cards.text: Half the kingdom on the table, and Esther picks a banquet. Friend, offer ME half a kingdom and I'm asking for the half with the ovens.

cards.question: When Esther invites them to her banquet, the king says there's no rush to bring Haman.

cards.text: So the king and Haman go to the banquet Esther prepared. As they drink their wine, the king asks her again what her petition is.

cards.question: At the banquet, the king once again offers Esther up to half the kingdom.
The king asks Esther again what she wants. What does she answer him at this first banquet?

answers.text: Come back tomorrow for another banquet
Cancel the law against the Jews
Send Haman away from the palace

cards.text: Tomorrow, she says, then she'll answer the king's question. One banquet down and the king STILL doesn't know what she wants, and I once waited forty minutes on a batch with the oven off, so I'm not judging anybody.
That day Haman walks out full of joy and glad of heart. Then he gets to the king's gate, and there's Mordecai.

cards.question: Haman walks past Mordecai at the king's gate. What does Mordecai do?

answers.text: He bows down to the ground
He gets up and walks away

cards.question: Seeing Mordecai at the gate, Haman goes from glad of heart to being filled with ___ toward Mordecai.
Haman lets his rage out on Mordecai right there at the king's gate.

cards.text: Haman holds it together, goes home and calls in his friends and his wife Zeresh. Then he reads them his own highlight reel: his glorious wealth, his many sons, and every way the king has honored and promoted him.

cards.question: Then Haman adds one more brag to the list. What is it?

answers.text: Only he was invited to Esther's banquet
The king named him governor of Susa
Esther asked him for his advice

cards.question: After all that bragging, Haman says none of it satisfies him as long as he sees ___ sitting at the king's gate.

cards.text: Wealth, sons, honor, a seat at the queen's banquet, and one man at a gate ruins ALL of it. That's me with a perfect batch of two dozen, staring at the ONE burnt cookie.
So his wife Zeresh and all his friends speak up. They've got advice for him.

cards.question: What do Zeresh and Haman's friends tell him to have built?

answers.text: A prison next to the gate
A tower over the city wall

cards.question: Zeresh and his friends tell Haman to ask the king in the morning to have Mordecai hanged. The advice pleases Haman, and he has the gallows built.

cards.text: Last step of their advice: go to the banquet with the king and enjoy himself. We'll leave it right there, friend, because this story is a long way from done.

findings.problem: The card says Mordecai has "begged" Queen Esther to plead with the king. Esther 4:8 says Mordecai sent the decree to Esther "to instruct her to approach the king, implore his favor, and plead with him on behalf of her people." The pleading is what Esther is told to do with the king. Mordecai instructs. He doesn't beg.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The card only restates card 7's answer ("Half the kingdom on the table, and Esther picks a banquet") and adds a joke. It tells nothing new from the passage, and card 7's question already said "With up to half the kingdom on the table."

The joke's action doesn't match the moment. Esther is offered up to half the kingdom and asks for something small, a banquet. In Papa Dorin's comparison he still takes half the kingdom ("the half with the ovens"), so it isn't the same action.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The question calls it "this first banquet." That tells the baker a second banquet is coming, which gives away the right answer ("Come back tomorrow for another banquet") and rules out the other two answers.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The joke's action doesn't match the moment. Esther puts off her answer on purpose and the king waits on her. In the comparison, Papa Dorin waits on a batch that will never bake because he left the oven off by mistake. Waiting for something that can't happen through your own mistake isn't the same action as the king waiting for Esther's request.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The card only restates what cards 5 to 7 already told (wealth, sons, honor, the banquet, Mordecai at the gate) and adds a joke. It tells nothing new from the passage.

Haman and Mordecai are named in the lesson without saying who they are, for example Haman as the king's top official or Mordecai as Esther's cousin. This is passage 5 of 10 in the Esther story group, so earlier lessons introduced them.
findings.question: In a passage that isn't the first in its story group, does "The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are" mean the first time in this lesson, or only the first time in the story group?
